resources.string: Get the score and the proof.
picai runs an open AI-detection model and reads every EXIF, C2PA, and IPTC field a photo is carrying \u2014 then hands you a clean copy with all of it stripped. No sign-up, no black box.

It reports a probability, not a verdict. Scores near 50% are labelled Uncertain; treat any single result as a signal and combine it with other evidence.
Does my image leave my computer?

On this public instance, yes: the picture is uploaded to the picai server (a Google Cloud Run container run by the author), scored in memory and never written to disk. The scrubbed copy is held in memory only until 100 newer results replace it or the container restarts, and nothing is sent to a third-party API. If you want nothing to leave your machine, run picai yourself with one Docker command.
Yes. The code, the Docker image, the CLI and the GitHub Action are all in the picai repository under the MIT licence. The detector is an open Hugging Face model you can inspect or replace.
Can I remove C2PA and other metadata?
Yes. After checking a picture, use Save clean copy. picai rebuilds the image from its pixels, so EXIF, XMP, IPTC, C2PA and the ICC profile are all left behind.
JPEG, PNG, WebP, HEIC/HEIF and most formats Pillow can decode, up to 50 MB.
C2PA content credentials and editing-software tags are provenance hints. The panel shows which blocks (EXIF, XMP, IPTC, C2PA, ICC) the file carries so you can weigh them alongside the score.
Can I use a different model?
Yes. Set PICAI_DETECTOR_MODEL to any Hugging Face image-classification model whose labels name AI/fake vs. human/real content.
Drop, paste or pick a picture. It is sent to the picai server you are using, held in memory and never written to disk.
An open-source image classifier scores how likely the pixels were produced by a generator.
You get an AI likelihood, a confidence band and the metadata blocks the file carries \u2014 as a probability, not a verdict.
